defaults.permitted_development: In Scotland there is no blanket right for a substantial 'temporary building' simply because it will be removed later. The clearest national flexibility is temporary use of land for up to 28 days in a calendar year; moveable structures associated with that use can stay on the land during that period but must be removed when the period ends. More fixed or longer-lived structures normally need planning permission.

rules.height_rules: There is no standard national height allowance for temporary buildings. Height is judged by whether the structure remains genuinely moveable and short lived or becomes operational development.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth limit. Duration, footprint, permanence, anchoring and service connections matter more than any single dimension.
rules.boundary_rules: Temporary rights are time limited and do not override controls on access, highway safety, nuisance or protected land. Leaving structures in place after the temporary period is likely to trigger planning control.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof rule. A substantial roofed enclosure is more likely to be treated as building work than as a simple temporary use.
rules.materials_rules: Use lightweight, reversible materials and details that support the temporary case. Heavy cladding, permanent-looking foundations and full services make the structure harder to treat as a short-term installation.

rules.permitted_development: In Scotland there is no blanket right for a substantial temporary building simply because it will be removed later. The clearest national flexibility is the temporary use of land for up to 28 days in a calendar year, with moveable structures allowed during that period only; beyond that, urban impacts such as servicing, crowding, noise and public realm pressure can quickly make a planning application necessary.

rules.height_rules: There is no standard national height allowance for temporary buildings. A taller or more engineered structure is more likely to be treated as operational development.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth limit. Duration, footprint, anchoring, service connections and the intensity of use matter more than any single dimension.
rules.boundary_rules: Temporary rights do not override controls on access, pedestrian safety, neighbour amenity, waste or licensed activities. In urban locations those practical issues often determine whether the proposal can proceed.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof rule. A fixed weatherproof enclosure or rigid frame is more likely to be treated as building work than a simple temporary feature.
rules.materials_rules: Use lightweight, reversible materials and details that support the temporary case. Heavy cladding, permanent-looking foundations and full services make the structure harder to treat as a short-term installation. In built-up areas, visibility from the street, servicing and noise can quickly undermine a claim that a structure is only a minor temporary feature.

restrictions.conservation_area: Temporary development in a conservation area should remain genuinely short term and reversible. Heritage impact can still justify a planning application.
restrictions.listed_building: Temporary works affecting a listed building or its setting may still need listed building consent and planning permission.

rules.permitted_development: In Scotland there is no blanket right for a substantial 'temporary building' simply because it will be removed later. The clearest national flexibility is temporary use of land for up to 28 days in a calendar year; moveable structures associated with that use can stay on the land during that period but must be removed when the period ends. More fixed or longer-lived structures normally need planning permission. On exposed or visitor-facing sites, anchoring, appearance and clutter can become bigger issues than the word temporary suggests.

rules.height_rules: There is no standard national height allowance for temporary buildings. Height is judged by whether the structure remains genuinely moveable and short lived or becomes operational development.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth limit. Duration, footprint, permanence, anchoring and service connections matter more than any single dimension.
rules.boundary_rules: Temporary rights are time limited and do not override controls on access, highway safety, nuisance or protected land. Leaving structures in place after the temporary period is likely to trigger planning control. On exposed or visitor-facing sites, anchoring, appearance and clutter can become bigger issues than the word temporary suggests.
rules.roof_rules: There is no separate roof rule. A substantial roofed enclosure is more likely to be treated as building work than as a simple temporary use.
rules.materials_rules: Use lightweight, reversible materials and details that support the temporary case. Heavy cladding, permanent-looking foundations and full services make the structure harder to treat as a short-term installation. On exposed or visitor-facing sites, anchoring, appearance and clutter can become bigger issues than the word temporary suggests.
